title: Graded alert suppression and solution handshake for PagerDuty + Slack
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Background: Our ops teams are drowning in noisy alerts (transient latency spikes, repeated traces that differ only by user-id). Existing suppression is binary (mute/unmute) and lacks context for responders. Goal: introduce a graded suppression model that reduces noisy PD/Slack alerts while surfacing an automated 'solution handshake' — a compact, pre-populated remediation bundle (runbook snippet + trace link + rollback/run command) attached to the incident notification.

Proposal:
- Graded suppression rules: severity buckets A/B/C derived from SLO breach magnitude, burst frequency, and historical true-positive rate. Each bucket maps to an escalation policy: C (suppress + webhook digest), B (suppress for 5m, create low-priority PD incident with solution bundle), A (immediate PD/Slack notify).
- Solution handshake: when creating an incident we attach: 1) a 2-3 line runbook snippet (from runbook store), 2) compact trace link (traceID + relevant spans) and top 3 correlated logs, 3) one-click remediation links (GitHub PR/rollback command or automation runbook trigger).
- Trace context: tracing hooks will populate compact context tokens (kv:trace_snippet) and a short causal graph image URL to include in Slack attachments. We will reuse existing trace extraction endpoints (ENG-611223 style) but add a concise serialization to reduce payload size.
- API/Integration changes: PD adapter will support 'suppression_level' and 'solution_handshake' fields. Slack attachments will include action buttons ("Apply Runbook", "Open Trace", "Join Triage") and an acknowledgement flow to record responder actions.

Trade-offs and risks:
- Risk of over-suppression: mitigated by conservative thresholds and immediate visibility in digest channels.
- Extra latency assembling solution bundles: create async pre-compute path (cache runbook snippets per alert signature).

Acceptance criteria:
- Noise volume (alerts/hour) from top noisy rule -> 50% reduction in non-actionable PD paging in first 30 days.
- Median time-to-first-action for suppressed-but-digest alerts improves by >=25% (measured via acknowledgement events).
- Solution handshake appears in PD incidents and Slack messages with correct trace links and runbook excerpts for 95% of sampled alerts.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary workspace): enable graded suppression for two noisy rules (query-level latency spike, 429 burst) and test handshake format in a private Slack channel. (2 weeks)
- Phase 2 (broader): enable on production with monitoring and automated rollback toggle. (2 weeks)
- Phase 3: add ML-based dedupe and historical scoring. (follow-up)

Metrics/observability: alerts/hour, PD pages avoided, median assemble-latency for handshake payload, click-throughs on remediation buttons, false-suppression incidents. Create dashboard in Console under "Incident Integrations > Suppression".

Docs and runbooks: PRD link: https://company-confluence/reports/obs/graded-suppression (placeholder), design mockups in Drive, SDK adapter changes in GH PR (TBD).
